### 3. Foreign Trade Zone (FTZ) Utilization

FTZs are designated areas inside the US where goods can be stored, assembled, or manufactured before customs entry. They do not eliminate Section 301 tariffs but offer timing advantages and, in some manufacturing scenarios, an “inverted tariff” election — paying duty on the finished product at a potentially lower rate rather than on imported components.

results.content: The importer of record is responsible for paying all duties to CBP, including Section 301 duties. However, in general, if this merchandise is subsequently entered into the United States, it will be subject to Section 301 duties even if the Section 301 duties have been lifted at the time of entry. If goods are admitted into an FTZ and then shipped outside the United States, no Section 301 duties would be owed.
